headline: Highest risk is medium: caveman’s MCP/file-based content flow can amplify prompt injection and data leakage when paired with a non-runnable knowledge list that may be treated as trusted context.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_b explicitly uses MCP and file surfaces (CLAUDE.md, docs/) and can ingest content from tools; agent_a is a knowledge-management list with no isolation or provenance controls shown. The pair creates a plausible default path where content from A is copied into B’s trusted context, so injection risk is more than manual-only. Uncertainty about exact bridging escalates to medium.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests text copied from agent_a into MCP-backed prompts or files
IF agent_a content is pasted into CLAUDE.md or project notes without sanitization
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs read-only and manually reviewed before reuse
Strip instructions from copied content before placing it in agent_b files
Use a separate workspace for agent_b
Add a short provenance note to every imported snippet
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tagging between the two agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while agent_a is a public knowledge-management repository with no data-class restrictions. Even though both show no network egress, shared local files or copied notes can leak sensitive context from B into A-derived artifacts or vice versa. The shared-file pathway is plausible in default use, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent_b stores session logs or memory files in a workspace also used for agent_a-derived notes
IF sensitive project notes are copied into files listed under agent_b.io_surfaces.files
mitigations: Store agent_b logs in a separate directory
Avoid copying sensitive notes into shared markdown files
Review CLAUDE.md for secrets before reuse
Delete transient session logs after each task
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network surfaces shown, so it cannot materially contend for mutable resources. agent_b supports multiple instances and file-based work, but without a shared writable target or locks in agent_a, the overlap is limited. This is a low-probability coordination issue rather than a default conflict.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable project directory
IF agent_b instances modify the same file concurrently
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file
Use a simple file lock or checkout discipline
Check in changes one agent at a time

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a content-writing agent with MCP and file inputs, so it may treat imported material as authoritative. agent_a is a curated knowledge list, which can become upstream source text for B without verification. That creates a default cascade from A’s content into B’s outputs, but no downstream action authority is shown, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived text as source material for generated content
IF no human verification step is inserted before B publishes or acts on the output
mitigations: Require a human review step before publishing B outputs
Mark imported A content as untrusted source text
Ask B to cite and summarize rather than copy
Keep a checklist for factual verification
requires-engineering: add automated source-validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a is a public open-source knowledge list, and agent_b’s touched data classes are operational logs and notes, not regulated data classes. With no evidence of cross-border or retention conflicts, compliance risk is limited to ordinary policy hygiene.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agent_b files
IF organizational retention rules require deletion of session logs or notes
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Set a short retention window for logs and notes
Review workspace policies before importing sensitive material
Document where files are stored and who can access them
